$comment: Canonical skill slots. 'owner_axis' names the axis whose selected fragment supplies the body. 'composite' slots additionally take contributions from other axes — via '<slot>#<anchor>' (injected at <% sections.<anchor> %>) or a bare '<slot>' (appended). 'emit_as' is declared per-fragment.

backend-models.$comment: The framework owns DTO shape and validation; the mapping axis supplies the entity->DTO section at the #mapping anchor.

backend-service.$comment: The framework owns the controller/service/module shape; the ORM supplies the data-access blocks via #provider and #crud_base. That split is what lets a new ORM drop in without forking the framework body.

backend-controller.$comment: The HTTP layer, for frameworks that separate it from the application service. NestJS folds controller, service and module into one backend-module skill and provides nothing here; ASP.NET Core splits them, because 'controllers stay thin' is only teachable when the two have separate homes.

backend-permissions.$comment: Owned by the authz axis; the backend framework supplies the framework-specific enforcement snippet at #enforcement.
